title: Predicting High-Salary AI Jobs in 2025
text: This project analyzes the Global AI Job Market & Salary Trends 2025 dataset to predict high-salary AI jobs (above the 75th percentile) using a Random Forest model. By identifying key factors like experience level and skills (e.g., Python), we provide insights for Pakistani professionals targeting lucrative remote roles. Built with R, tidyverse, and tidymodels, this report is published as a GitHub Page, showcasing data cleaning, machine learning, and interactive visualizations for a data science portfolio.

title: Predicting High-Salary AI Jobs in 2025
text:
Setup
We use R with tidyverse for data processing, Plotly for interactive visualizations, and tidymodels for modeling. The dataset (ai_job_dataset1.csv) is assumed to be in the working directory.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)
library(purrr)
library(tidymodels)
library(vip)

# Verify file exists
if (!file.exists("ai_job_dataset1.csv")) {
  stop("Error: ai_job_dataset1.csv not found.")
}

# Load data
df <- read_csv("ai_job_dataset1.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Check if df is a data frame
if (!is.data.frame(df)) {
  stop("Error: read_csv did not return a data frame.")
}

# Clean data
df_cleaned <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(job_id), !is.na(salary_usd), !is.na(experience_level)) %>%
  mutate(
    salary_usd = as.numeric(salary_usd),
    years_experience = as.numeric(years_experience),
    remote_ratio = as.numeric(remote_ratio),
    benefits_score = as.numeric(benefits_score),
    required_skills = str_split(required_skills, ",\\s*"),
    required_skills = map(required_skills, ~str_trim(.x)),
    required_skills = map(required_skills, ~.x[.x != ""])
  ) %>%
  filter(salary_usd > 0)

# Verify cleaned data
if (nrow(df_cleaned) == 0) {
  stop("Error: No rows remain after cleaning.")
}

title: Predicting High-Salary AI Jobs in 2025
text:
Predicting High-Salary AI Jobs
We use a Random Forest model to predict whether a job offers a high salary (above the 75th percentile), identifying key factors like experience level, skills, and location. Interactive visualizations include a confusion matrix heatmap and a prediction probability histogram


Code
# Prepare data
set.seed(123)
high_salary_threshold <- quantile(df_cleaned$salary_usd, 0.75)
df_model <- df_cleaned %>%
  mutate(
    high_salary = as.factor(ifelse(salary_usd > high_salary_threshold, "Yes", "No")),
    has_python = map_lgl(required_skills, ~"Python" %in% .x),
    has_sql = map_lgl(required_skills, ~"SQL" %in% .x),
    has_aws = map_lgl(required_skills, ~"AWS" %in% .x)
  ) %>%
  select(high_salary, experience_level, years_experience, remote_ratio, company_location, has_python, has_sql, has_aws, benefits_score) %>%
  drop_na()

# Split data
split <- initial_split(df_model, prop = 0.8, strata = high_salary)
train_data <- training(split)
test_data <- testing(split)

# Define Random Forest model
rf_spec <- rand_forest(trees = 100, mode = "classification") %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity")

# Create workflow
rf_workflow <- workflow() %>%
  add_model(rf_spec) %>%
  add_formula(high_salary ~ .)

# Fit model
rf_fit <- rf_workflow %>%
  fit(data = train_data)

# Evaluate model
predictions <- rf_fit %>%
  predict(test_data, type = "prob") %>%
  bind_cols(predict(rf_fit, test_data)) %>%
  bind_cols(test_data) %>%
  mutate(high_salary = as.factor(high_salary))

# Confusion matrix data
conf_matrix <- predictions %>%
  conf_mat(truth = high_salary, estimate = .pred_class) %>%
  tidy() %>%
  mutate(
    Actual = case_when(
      str_detect(name, "^T") ~ "High Salary",  # TP, TN
      str_detect(name, "^F") ~ "Not High Salary"  # FP, FN
    ),
    Predicted = case_when(
      name %in% c("TP", "FP") ~ "High Salary",
      name %in% c("TN", "FN") ~ "Not High Salary"
    )
  )

# Interactive confusion matrix heatmap
fig_conf_matrix <- plot_ly(
  data = conf_matrix,
  x = ~Predicted,
  y = ~Actual,
  z = ~value,
  type = "heatmap",
  colorscale = list(
    list(0, "#f7f7f7"),
    list(1, "#ff7f0e")
  ),
  hovertemplate = "Actual: %{y}<br>Predicted: %{x}<br>Count: %{z}<extra></extra>"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Confusion Matrix for High-Salary Prediction", x = 0.5),
    xaxis = list(title = "Predicted"),
    yaxis = list(title = "Actual")
  )

# Prediction probability distribution
fig_prob_dist <- plot_ly(
  data = predictions,
  x = ~.pred_Yes,
  type = "histogram",
  marker = list(color = "#1f77b4"),
  hovertemplate = "Probability: %{x:.2f}<br>Count: %{y}<extra></extra>"
) %>%
  layout(
    title = list(text = "Distribution of Predicted Probabilities for High-Salary Jobs", x = 0.5),
    xaxis = list(title = "Predicted Probability of High Salary", range = c(0, 1)),
    yaxis = list(title = "Count")
  )

# Display outputs
fig_conf_matrix

Figure 1: Confusion matrix heatmap showing true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives for the model’s predictions. Figure 2: Histogram of predicted probabilities, indicating the model’s confidence in classifying high-salary jobs.

title: Predicting High-Salary AI Jobs in 2025
text:
Conclusion
The Random Forest model identifies experience level, Python skills, and company location as key predictors of high-salary AI jobs in 2025. For Pakistani professionals, mastering Python and targeting remote roles in high-paying markets like the US can lead to lucrative opportunities. This project demonstrates proficiency in R, tidyverse, tidymodels, and Plotly, making it a strong addition to a data science portfolio.
